title: Functorial square completions imply homotopy calculus of fractions
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,W)$ be a category with a wide subcategory as in [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus], with $W$ satisfying two-out-of-three: if two of $f,g,gf$ lie in $W$, the third does also. Let $U,V\subseteq W$ be wide subcategories. Suppose the following choices are functorial in commuting maps of their input diagrams. For every span $X'\xleftarrow{u}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ with $u\in U$, there are $g:X'\to Y'$ and $v:Y\to Y'$ with $v\in U$ and $gu=vf$; whenever $f\in W$, also $g\in W$. For every cospan $X\xrightarrow{g}Y\xleftarrow{v}Y'$ with $v\in V$, there are $u:X'\to X$ and $f:X'\to Y'$ with $u\in V$ and $gu=vf$; whenever $g\in W$, also $f\in W$. Finally every $w:A\to B$ in $W$ has a functorial factorization $A\xrightarrow{u}E\xrightarrow{v}B$ with $u\in U$, $v\in V$, and $vu=w$. Then $(\mathcal C,W)$ admits the two-sided homotopy calculus of fractions defined in [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus].
